current_route.title: Quarter-Wave Initialized Optimization and Order Verification
current_route.scientific_hypothesis: The global minimum for mean reflectance in this constrained two-layer system occurs with the SiO2 layer adjacent to air and the TiO2 layer adjacent to glass, with thicknesses perturbed slightly from the ideal quarter-wave values (SiO2 ~99nm, TiO2 ~60nm) to balance the broadband response. The reverse order (TiO2/SiO2) cannot achieve a lower mean reflectance even with optimal thickness tuning due to the impedance mismatch profile at the air interface.
current_route.design_principle: Impedance matching via graded index profile (Air -> Low Index -> High Index -> Glass) approximates a smoother transition than the reverse, reducing Fresnel reflections. Quarter-wave thicknesses provide zero reflectance at a specific design wavelength; optimizing around these values broadens the low-reflectance band across 450-700 nm.
current_route.proposed_topology: Two distinct fixed topologies evaluated in parallel: (1) Air | SiO2 | TiO2 | Glass and (2) Air | TiO2 | SiO2 | Glass. Total finite layers: 2.
design_variables: Stack ordering (discrete choice between the two defined topologies)
soft_objectives: Minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance (450-700 nm)
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness bounds strictly enforced between 40 nm and 160 nm
theory_basis: Quarter-wave condition: d = lambda_center / (4 * n). For lambda_center = 575 nm, d_SiO2 ≈ 98.5 nm, d_TiO2 ≈ 59.9 nm.
Fresnel equations dictate that placing the lower index material first reduces the initial air-interface reflection coefficient compared to placing the high index material first.
expected_advantages: Initialization near the physical optimum reduces the risk of the optimizer converging to a shallow local minimum far from the quarter-wave solution.
Explicitly testing the reverse order with equal optimization effort provides a definitive comparison rather than relying on potentially under-optimized baseline results from Round 1.
known_risks: The optimal solution might lie at the boundary of the thickness constraints (40 or 160 nm) if the quarter-wave condition is incompatible with the broadband requirement.
The discrete nature of the stack order means the optimizer must evaluate both topologies; if the search budget is split too thinly, one order might be under-explored.
current_route.execution_request_english: Execute a deterministic TMM optimization for a planar two-layer antireflection coating on a glass substrate (n=1.52) with air incidence (n=1.0). The stack must consist of exactly one SiO2 layer (n=1.46) and one TiO2 layer (n=2.40). Evaluate two fixed topologies: Topology A (Air|SiO2|TiO2|Glass) and Topology B (Air|TiO2|SiO2|Glass). For each topology, optimize the layer thicknesses within the range [40, 160] nm to minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance for s-polarized light at normal incidence over the wavelength range 450-700 nm (5 nm steps). Initialize the optimizer with seed 17. For Topology A, include initial guess points near the quarter-wave thicknesses (SiO2=99 nm, TiO2=60 nm) and their immediate neighbors. For Topology B, use a uniform grid initialization. Allow a maximum of 64 solver evaluations total across both topologies. Report the best thickness pair and mean reflectance for each topology, and identify the global best candidate. Canonical user controls: incidence angles 0 degrees. polarization s. wavelength intervals 450-700 nm. soft objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance from 450 nm to 700 nm; achieve mean reflectance below 0.03 as a soft scoring preference. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high reflection in the 450 nm to 700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: layer thickness must be between 40 nm and 160 nm; exactly one layer of SiO2 and one layer of TiO2.
current_route.revision_reason: Round 1 results showed a best score of 0.93 but lacked focused exploration around the theoretically optimal quarter-wave thicknesses. The feedback directive explicitly requests testing near SiO2 ~99nm and TiO2 ~60nm and confirming the superiority of the SiO2-first order. This route adjusts the initialization strategy to target these physical insights while maintaining the same hard constraints and objectives.
